h: Bereishit and the Three Foundations of Creation
The opening word of the Torah contains creation and points toward reverence, the covenant, and Shabbat.
All Creation Is Contained in Bereishit

p: בְּרֵאשִׁית:
In the beginning:
בְּתֵיבַת "בְּרֵאשִׁית" נִכְלָל כָּל מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית,
Within the word Bereishit is encapsulated the entirety of the Work of Creation,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמָּצִינוּ (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא)
just as we find (Bereishit Rabbah, parashah 11)
מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁנִּבְרָא בְּשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית,
regarding everything that was created during the six days of Creation, "
מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית" וְכַדּוֹמֶה,
terms such as 'the Work of Creation' and the like,
הַכֹּל נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם בְּרֵאשִׁית.
everything being designated by the name Bereishit.
וְהַטַּעַם, שֶׁהַכֹּל נִבְרָא בְּמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית",
And the rationale is that everything was brought into existence through the utterance Bereishit,
דִּ"בְּרֵאשִׁית" נַמֵּי מַאֲמָר הוּא (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב.),
for Bereishit is likewise an utterance (as written in Rosh Hashanah 32a),
וְאַחַר כָּךְ נַעֲשָׂה כָּל אֶחָד בִּזְמַנּוֹ.
and subsequently each individual creation was actualized at its appointed time.
וּבְאוֹרַיְיתָא בָּרָא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עָלְמָא,
And through the Torah, the Holy One, blessed be He, created the universe,
וּמִמֵּילָא נִכְלַל כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ גַּם כֵּן בְּמַאֲמַר "בְּרֵאשִׁית".
and consequently the entirety of the Torah is likewise incorporated within the utterance Bereishit.
וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי בְּתִקּוּנֵי הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ דָּרַשׁ שִׁבְעִין אַנְפִּין בְּתֵיבַת "בְּרֵאשִׁית",
And Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in Tikkunei HaZohar expounded seventy facets upon the word Bereishit,
וְהַיְינוּ כְּלַל הַתּוֹרָה,
which represents the sum total of the Torah,
כִּי שִׁבְעִים פָּנִים לַתּוֹרָה.
for 'there are seventy facets to the Torah.'
וְאִיתָא בְּתִקּוּנֵי הַזֹּהַר תְּלָת פִּקּוּדִין בְּמִלַּת "בְּרֵאשִׁית":
And it is taught in Tikkunei HaZohar that there are three commandments latent within the word Bereishit:
אֶחָד: יִרְאַת ה', כְּגַוְונָא דָא "יָרֵא בֹּשֶׁת" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סוֹף תִּקּוּן ו);
first: the fear of Hashem, according to this anagram 'reveres with shame' (yarei boshet; as written at the end of Tikkun 6);
שְׁנַיִם: בְּרִית, כְּגַוְונָא דָא בְּרֵאשִׁית – "בְּרִית אֵשׁ" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּהַקְדָּמָה וְתִקּוּן כג);
second: the covenant (brit), according to this permutation Bereishit – 'a covenant of fire' (brit eish; as written in the Introduction and Tikkun 23);
שְׁלֹשָׁה: שַׁבָּת, כְּגַוְונָא דָא "יָרֵא שַׁבָּת".
third: Shabbat, according to this anagram 'reveres the Sabbath' (yarei Shabbat).
וְהַתְּלָת פִּקּוּדִין הַלָּלוּ הֵם מְכֻוָּון כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה,
And these three commandments constitute the deliberate intention of all Creation,
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מְקֻדָּשִׁים בָּהֶם.
and Israel are sanctified through them.

h: From Fear of Punishment to Reverence Before Hashem

p: דִּבְיִרְאָה יֵשׁ יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים,
For within fear there is the fear of God (yirat Elohim),
וְהַיְינוּ יִרְאַת עֹנֶשׁ,
which is the lower dread of retribution,
וְיִרְאָה זוֹ אֵינֶנָּה תַּכְלִית מְכֻוָּון הַבְּרִיאָה,
and this category of fear is not the ultimate purpose of Creation,
שֶׁמָּצִינוּ גַּם בְּאַנְשֵׁי נִינְוֵה: "וַיִּתְכַּסּוּ שַׂקִּים וְגוֹמֵר מִי יוֹדֵעַ יָשׁוּב וְגוֹמֵר",
as we find even concerning the inhabitants of Nineveh: 'and they covered themselves with sackcloth, etc., who knows, He may turn, etc.,'
רַק הָיָה יִרְאַת הָעֹנֶשׁ לְבַדָּהּ,
where it was exclusively the fear of punishment alone,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְשָׁב מֵחֲרוֹן אַפּוֹ וְלֹא נֹאבֵד".
as it is stated: 'and turn away from His fierce anger, that we perish not.'
וְהוּא מִטַּעַם כִּי הֵיצַר לָהֶם עַל תַּעֲנוּגֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁלֹּא יֹאבְדוּ מֵהֶם.
And this was because they grieved over the physical pleasures of this world lest they be forfeited from them.
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ, בִּרְאוֹתוֹ שֶׁשְּׁאָלוּהוּ אִשְׁתּוֹ אוֹ אֲחוֹתוֹ הִיא,
And our father Abraham, upon observing that they interrogated him as to whether she was his wife or his sister,
אָמַר לַאֲבִימֶלֶךְ: "כִּי אָמַרְתִּי רַק אֵין יִרְאַת אֱלֹהִים בַּמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה",
said unto Abimelech: 'Because I thought: surely there is no fear of God in this place,'
כִּי הָאֻמּוֹת גָּדְרוּ עַצְמָן אַחַר הַמַּבּוּל מִיִּרְאַת עֹנֶשׁ.
for the pagan nations restrained themselves after the Deluge strictly out of fear of punishment.
וְאָמְנָם יִרְאַת ה' לֹא נִמְצָא רַק בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל,
However, true reverent awe of Hashem (yirat Havayah) is found solely within Israel,
וְהַיְינוּ יִרְאַת בֹּשֶׁת,
namely the fear of shame and embarrassment before His majesty,
כִּי זֶה הוּא עִיקַּר הַמְּכֻוָּון בְּהַבְּרִיאָה שֶׁיִּירְאוּ מִלְּפָנָיו.
for this constitutes the primary objective of Creation: that beings revere before Him.
וְאִיתָא (נְדָרִים כ.):
And it is brought (Nedarim 20a): "'
בַּעֲבוּר תִּהְיֶה יִרְאָתוֹ עַל פְּנֵיכֶם' – זוֹ בּוּשָׁה,
''That His fear may be upon your faces' – this refers to shame, '
לְבִלְתִּי תֶחֱטָאוּ' וְכוּלֵי,
'so that you do not sin, etc.,'
כָּל אָדָם הַמִּתְבַּיֵּישׁ לֹא בִּמְהֵרָה הוּא חוֹטֵא".
any man who possesses shame will not readily sin.'
וְאִיתָא (רֵישׁ הַגָּהַת שֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ אֹרַח חַיִּים):
And it is taught (at the opening gloss of the Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim):
כְּשֶׁיָּשִׂים הָאָדָם אֶל לִבּוֹ שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, אֲשֶׁר מְלֹא כָל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ, עֹמֵד עָלָיו וְרוֹאֶה בְּמַעֲשָׂיו וְכוּלֵי,
when a person sets into his heart that the supreme King, the Holy One, blessed be He, Whose glory fills the whole earth, stands over him and beholds his actions, etc.,
מִיָּד יַגִּיעַ אֵלָיו הַיִּרְאָה וְהַהַכְנָעָה בְּפַחַד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּבוֹשְׁתּוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ תָּמִיד.
immediately awe and humble submissiveness will envelop him in fear of Hashem, blessed be He, and he will constantly feel shame before Him.
וְאָמְרוּ (שָׁם נְדָרִים כ.):
And our Sages expounded (there, Nedarim 20a):
מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בֹּשֶׁת פָּנִים בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁלֹּא עָמְדוּ אֲבוֹתָיו עַל הַר סִינַי.
whoever lacks shamefacedness, it is known that his forebears did not stand at Mount Sinai.
כִּי בְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הָיוּ הַכֹּל,
For at the Giving of the Torah all were present,
אֲפִילּוּ הַנְּשָׁמוֹת שֶׁעֲתִידִין לְהִבָּרְאוֹת,
even the souls destined to be born into physical bodies in future generations,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא יִתְרוֹ יא) עַל פָּסוּק "וְאֵת אֲשֶׁר אֵינֶנּוּ פֹּה עִמָּנוּ הַיּוֹם",
as they expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Yitro 11) on the verse 'and with him that is not here with us this day,'
וְכֻלָּם רָאוּ אֶת כְּבוֹדוֹ וְאֶת גָּדְלוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
and all beheld His glory and His magnificent greatness, blessed be His Name,
וּמִמֵּילָא יֵשׁ לָהֶם יִרְאַת בֹּשֶׁת.
and consequently they possess an intrinsic sense of holy shame.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת כח:):
And as they stated (Berakhot 28b): "
יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁתְּהֵא מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם עֲלֵיכֶם כְּמוֹרָא בָּשָׂר וָדָם",
'May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood,'
כִּי הָרוֹאֶה פְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁחָטָא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מִתְבַּיֵּישׁ מֵאִתּוֹ,
for one who sees the face of a human being against whom he has sinned is ashamed before him,
וּכְמוֹ כֵן יִהְיֶה מוֹרָא שָׁמַיִם עֲלֵיכֶם,
and so too may the fear of Heaven be upon you,

paragraphs.text: Midrash Tanchuma, Yitro 11:1: “And God spoke all these words, saying: “I am the Lord thy God” (Exod. 20:1). R. Isaac said: All the prophets received the inspirations for their future prophesies at Mount Sinai. How do we know this to be so? It is written: But with him that standeth here with us this day before the Lord our God, and also with him that is not here with us this day (Deut. 29:14). That standeth here with us this day refers to those who were already born, and with him that is not here alludes to those who were to be born in the future. Hence they are not with us this day. “Not standing here with us this day” is not written in this verse, but rather Is not here with us this day. This alludes to the souls who were to be created in the future, since standing here could not be said of them. They were included in the general statement. And that is why the verse states: The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by Malachi (Mal. 1:1). It does not say “of Malachi,” but merely by Malachi, indicating that the prophecy had been transmitted to him previously at Sinai. Similarly Isaiah said: Come ye near unto Me, hear ye this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time that it was, there am I; and now the Lord hath sent me, and His spirit (Isa. 48:16). Isaiah is saying here that at the time the Torah was given I received the prophecy. Hence it says: from the time that it (the Torah) was, there am I; and now the Lord God hath sent me, and His spirit, but until now He did not give me permission to prophesy.”

Mesillat Yesharim 24:6-8: “The second kind is awe of His exaltedness: a person distances himself from sins and refrains from committing them because of the great honor of His blessed Name. How could lowly, insignificant flesh and blood profane that honor, or dare to do something contrary to the will of the Creator, blessed and exalted be His Name?

This awe is not so easy to attain. It arises only from knowledge and understanding, through contemplating His exaltedness and the lowliness of man. All of these are products of an intellect that understands and reflects. This is the awe that we identified as the second part of one of the branches of piety discussed earlier.

Through it, a person feels shame and trembles when standing before his Maker to pray or perform any act of service. This is the praiseworthy awe for which the pious of every age were praised. It is what Moshe speaks of when he says (Devarim 28:58), “To fear this honored and awesome Name, Hashem your God.””

h: Brit Eish: The Covenant and the Struggle Against Desire

p: וְכֵן "בְּרִית אֵשׁ",
So too is the second anagram Brit Eish ('Covenant of Fire'),
כִּי תַּכְלִית מְכֻוָּון הַבְּרִיאָה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן עֲבוּר שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית,
for the primary aim of Creation was likewise for the preservation of the sacred Covenant,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְצַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם".
as it is stated (Proverbs 10:25): 'and the righteous is the foundation of the world.'
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א, צג עַמּוּד א),
And as written in the holy Zohar (Part I, 93a),
דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִתְגְּזַר, שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה,
that once an Israelite is circumcised on the eighth day,
אֲנַחְנוּ מְדוּבָּקִים בִּקְדוּשָּׁה בַּשּׁוֹרֶשׁ,
we are bound inseparably to divine holiness at the root,
וּרְצוֹנֵנוּ רַק לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,
and our true desire is solely to perform His will, blessed be He,
וּלְזֶה נִקְרְאוּ "צַדִּיקִים".
and therefore the Jewish people are titled Tzaddikim ('righteous').
וְאַף אִם יֵשׁ אַחַר כָּךְ אֵיזֶה חִסָּרוֹן,
And even if thereпоследствии arises some moral failing,
הוּא רַק מִצַּד הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה.
it stems solely from the external leaven in the dough (the evil inclination).
כִּי כָּל הַתַּאֲווֹת שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא רַק מִצַּד עֲמָלֵקִים
For all base passions found among Israel arise solely from the spiritual forces of Amalek,

וְתָמִיד אֲנַחְנוּ נִלְחָמִים נֶגֶד הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
and we are continuously battling against the evil inclination,

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 6:6: “Where are the orbs of the sun and the moon situated? They are in the second firmament, as it is stated: “God set them in the firmament of the heavens.” Rabbi Pinḥas said in the name of Rabbi Abahu: There is an explicit verse, and the members of the Great Assembly elaborated on it: “You, the Lord, alone, You made the heavens, the heaven of heavens, and all their host…” (Nehemiah 9:6). Where is all their host situated? It is in the firmament that is above the heavens. From the earth to the firmament is a distance of five hundred years’ walk, and the thickness of the firmament is a distance of five hundred years’ walk, and from firmament to firmament is a distance of five hundred years’ walk. See how high it is. And we learned, on the first day of the summer solstice, there is no shade for any creature, as it is written: “Nothing can shelter from its heat” (Psalms 19:7). The orb of the sun has a sheath, as it is stated: “In a tent within, He placed the sun” (Psalms 19:5), and there is a pool of water before it. When it emerges [from the sheath], the Holy One blessed be He mitigates its strength through that water so that it should not emerge and incinerate the world. But in the future, the Holy One blessed be He will strip it of its sheath and burn the wicked with it, as it is stated: “The day that is coming will burn them” (Malachi 3:19). Rabbi Yanai and Rabbi Shimon both say: There will be no Gehenna [in the future]; rather, there will be a [scorching] day that will burn up the wicked. What is the source? “For, behold, the day is coming, burning like a furnace…” (Malachi 3:19). The Rabbis say: There will be a Gehenna, as it is stated: “The utterance of the Lord, for whom there is fire in Zion…” (Isaiah 31:9). Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai says: There will be neither a [scorching] day nor a Gehenna, but rather, a fire that emerges from the body of the wicked themselves and burns them. What is the source? It is as it is written: “Conceive stubble, give birth to straw, your spirit is a fire that will consume you” (Isaiah 33:11). Rabbi Yehoshua bar Avin said: “The heavens will declare His beneficence” (Psalms 50:6) – in the future, the heavens will relate the beneficence that the Holy One blessed be He bestowed upon His world, in that He did not situate them in the first firmament. Had He situated them in the first firmament, no creature could have withstood the fire of the day.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 48:8: ““At the entrance [petaḥ] of the tent [ohel]” – [God said to Abraham:] ‘You opened a good opening [petaḥ] for passersby, you opened a good opening for proselytes. [Moreover,] were it not for you, I would not have created heaven and earth, as it is stated regarding them: “He stretched them like a tent for dwelling” (Isaiah 40:22). Were it not for you, I would not have created the orb of the sun, as it is stated: “In a tent within, He placed the sun” (Psalms 19:5). Were it not for you, I would not have created the moon, as it is stated: “Behold, even the moon does not shine [yaahil]”’ (Job 25:5). Rabbi Levi said: In the future, Abraham will sit at the entrance of Gehenna and will not allow any circumcised person of Israel to descend into it. But those who sinned greatly, what does he do to them? He removes the foreskin from babies who died before they were circumcised, and he places it upon them, and sends them down to Gehenna. That is what is written: “He raised his arms against his comrades, violating his covenant” (Psalms 55:21). “In the heat of the day” – when that day will come in whose regard it is written: “For, behold, the day is coming, burning like an oven” (Malachi 3:19). “In the heat of the day” – Rabbi Yishmael taught: “In the heat of the day” – this is speaking of the sixth hour [of the day.] How then do I explain [the verse regarding the manna]: “The sun grew hot and it melted”? (Exodus 16:21). It is at the fourth hour. You say that it is the fourth hour, but perhaps it is really at the sixth hour? When it says: “In the heat of the day” – that [expression] is speaking of the sixth hour. Or, perhaps it is the reverse, “in the heat of the day” refers to the fourth hour, and “the sun grew hot and it melted” refers to the sixth hour. You must admit, however: How can you explain “in the heat of the day” to be the fourth hour? Is it not so that at the fourth hour, the heat is only in a place where the sun shines? At the fourth hour, the shade is cool while the sun is hot. At the sixth hour, the shade and the sun are equally hot. Therefore, you should not say in accordance with the second formulation, but rather like the first formulation: “In the heat of the day” refers to the sixth hour, and “the sun grew hot and it melted” refers to the fourth hour, as only in the place where the sun shone did it melt. Rabbi Tanḥuma says: It [the sixth hour] is at a time when people do not have a shadow at the bottom of them. Rabbi Yanai said: He pierced a hole from Gehenna and heated up the entire world along with its inhabitants for a brief moment, for the Holy One blessed be He said: ‘The righteous are suffering and the world is comfortable?’ This teaches that heat is effective for a wound.”

Rabbi Yanai said: He pierced a hole from Gehenna and heated up the entire world along with its inhabitants for a brief moment, for the Holy One blessed be He said: ‘The righteous are suffering and the world is comfortable?’ This teaches that heat is effective for a wound.”

h: Shabbat: The Third Sanctity of Creation

p: תְּלִיתָאֵי: "שַׁבָּת יָרֵא".
The third permutation is Shabbat Yarei ('reveres the Sabbath').
וּקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת הוּא גַּם כֵּן רַק לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And the holiness of Shabbat is likewise reserved exclusively for Israel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי אוֹת הִוא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם",
as it is stated (Exodus 31:13): 'for it is a sign between Me and you,'
וְעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת שֶׁשָּׁבַת חַיָּיב,
and an idolater who observes Shabbat is liable to death,
כִּי אֵין לָהֶם שַׁיָּיכוּת כְּלָל לִקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
for they have no connection whatsoever to the sanctity of the Sabbath;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה דְּבָרִים א, כא):
and as they stated in Midrash Rabbah (Devarim 1:21):
לְמֶלֶךְ וּמַטְרוֹנָה יוֹשְׁבִים וּמְשִׂיחִין זֶה עִם זֶה, מִי שֶׁבָּא וּמַכְנִיס עַצְמוֹ בֵּינֵיהֶם וְכוּלֵי.
a parable of a king and queen sitting and conversing intimately together; whoever comes and intrudes between them is liable to execution.
וְשַׁבָּת הִיא תַּכְלִית כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה,
And Shabbat is the ultimate purpose of all Creation,
וְהִיא כּוֹלֶלֶת כָּל הַתְּלָת פִּקּוּדִין,
and it synthesizes all three of these commandments,
כִּי הַשּׁוֹמֵר שַׁבָּת נִקְרָא "יָרֵא",
for one who guards Shabbat is called 'one who reveres,'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁדָּרְשׁוּ (תַּעֲנִית ח:): "'יִרְאֵי שְׁמִי' – עַל שׁוֹמְרֵי שַׁבָּת".
as they expounded (Ta'anit 8b): ''Those who revere My Name'—this refers to the guardians of Shabbat.'
וְאָמְרוּ (יְרוּשַׁלְמִי פֶּרֶק ד דִּדְמַאי): "אֵימַת שַׁבָּת עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ",
And they taught (Yerushalmi Demai 4:1): 'The dread of Shabbat rests even upon an unlearned person (am ha'aretz),'
וּכְאִלּוּ רוֹאֶה מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עוֹמֵד עָלָיו כָּל הַשַּׁבָּת
as though he actually sees the King of kings standing over him throughout the entire Sabbath
וְיָרֵא מִמֶּנּוּ שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּשֵׁל חָלִילָה בְּאִיסּוּר שַׁבָּת.
and is filled with awe before Him lest he stumble, Heaven forbid, into any Sabbath prohibition.
וְגַם שַׁבָּת נִקְרָא "אוֹת" וְנִקְרָא "בְּרִית",
Furthermore, Shabbat is termed an 'ot' (sign) and termed a 'brit' (covenant),
דְּשַׁבָּת בְּרָזָא דִּבְרִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ.
for Shabbat is aligned within the mystical secret of the Covenant (Yesod), as written in the holy Zohar.

h: The Three Shabbat Meals and the Patriarchs

p: וְהַשָּׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת הֵם כְּנֶגֶד שְׁלֹשֶׁת הָאָבוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים
And the three meals on Shabbat correspond to the three holy Patriarchs,
שֶׁהֵם שׁוֹרֶשׁ מֵהַתְּלָת פִּקּוּדִין.
who are the living roots of these three commandments.
וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ נִקְרָא "יָרֵא",
Our father Abraham is titled 'one who reveres,'
כִּי רָאָה תָּמִיד מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹמֵד עָלָיו וְרוֹאֶה בְּמַעֲשָׂיו,
for he constantly perceived the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, standing over him and observing his actions,
כִּי לֹא הָיָה לוֹ רַב שֶׁיְּלַמְּדוֹ
since he had no mortal teacher to instruct him,
רַק הִתְחִיל מֵעַצְמוֹ לַחְקוֹר: "תֹּאמַר שֶׁהַבִּירָה זוֹ בְּלֹא מַנְהִיג וְכוּלֵי"
rather he began investigating on his own: 'Can one say that this illuminated palace lacks a guide, etc.'
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה,
as written in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 39),
וּמִכָּל מַה שֶּׁנִּבְרָא בָּעוֹלָם רָאָה כִּי מַעֲשֵׂי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵמָּה,
and from everything created within the cosmos he perceived that they are the handiwork of Hashem, blessed be He,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהָיוּ עֵינֶיךָ רֹאוֹת אֶת מוֹרֶיךָ",
and as it is stated (Isaiah 30:20): 'and your eyes shall see your Teacher,'
וְרָאָה אֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִכָּל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּבְרָא בָּעוֹלָם.
and he discerned Hashem, blessed be He, through every detail created in existence.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שֶׁנִּרְאָה לָאָבוֹת בְּשֵׁם "אֵל שַׁדַּי",
And this is why Scripture notes that He appeared unto the Patriarchs by the Name El Shaddai,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רַבֵּינוּ רַבִּי בּוּנֶם זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
and as our master Rabbi Simcha Bunim taught,
דְּשֵׁם זֶה מְרַמֵּז עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יב.):
that this divine Name alludes to what they stated (Chagigah 12a): "
אֲנִי הוּא שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי לָעוֹלָם דַּי",
'I am He Who said unto the world: Enough (dai)!'
שֶׁהָיָה הָעוֹלָם מַרְחִיב וְהוֹלֵךְ וְכוּלֵי עַד שֶׁנָּעַר בּוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהֶעֱמִידוֹ.
for the universe was expanding boundlessly outward until the Holy One rebuked it and brought it to a stand.
הַיְינוּ, כִּי הַבְּרִיאָה הָיְתָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיַּכִּירוּ הַנִּבְרָאִים אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
That is to say: Creation occurred solely so that created beings would recognize His divinity, blessed be His Name,
וְאָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא "דַּי",
and the Holy One said unto them 'Enough',
שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכִים לְהִתְמַתֵּחַ עוֹד יוֹתֵר,
meaning that the dimensions need not stretch any further,
כִּי תַּסְפִּיק הַבְּרִיאָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁהִיא לְהַכִּיר מִמֶּנָּה אֱלֹהוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ.
because Creation as it stands is fully sufficient to deduce and recognize His Godliness through it.
וּמִמֵּילָא, כְּשֶׁהִכִּיר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ מֵהַבְּרִיאָה אֱלֹהוּתוֹ,
And consequently, when our father Abraham recognized His divinity directly from Creation,
הָיָה רוֹאֶה מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עוֹמֵד עָלָיו.
he continually perceived the King of kings standing over him.
וְזֶה זָכָה עַל יְדֵי הַמִּילָה,
And this vision he merited specifically through circumcision,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּרָא מז, ז) שֶׁאָמַר אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם:
as written (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashat Vayeira 47:7) that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, said: "
אִלּוּלֵי הַמִּילָה מֵהֵיכָן הָיָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִגְלֶה עָלַי, 'וּמִבְּשָׂרִי אֶחֱזֶה אֱלוֹהַּ'".
'Were it not for circumcision, whence would the Holy One have revealed Himself unto me, as in 'and from my flesh I shall behold God' (Job 19:26).'
וְזָכָה לִהְיוֹת אֶזְרָח בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל אַף שֶׁלֹּא נוֹלַד בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
And he merited to become the native citizen (ezrach) of Israel even though he was not originally born in holiness,
כִּי עַל יְדֵי מִילָה נִתְקַשֵּׁר בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ עַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת וּתְפִיסַת שֵׂכֶל אֱנוֹשִׁי,
because through circumcision he became bound to the primordial supernal Root (Atika) which transcends human intellect,
וְרָאָה מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים עוֹמֵד עָלָיו,
and he perceived the King of kings standing over him,
וְהָיָה "יָרֵא בֹּשֶׁת" כָּאָמוּר.
and stood in 'awe of shame' (yarei boshet) as stated.

h: Yitzchak and the Sanctity of the Covenant

p: וְיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה כְּנֶגֶד "בְּרִית אֵשׁ",
And our father Isaac, peace be upon him, corresponds to Brit Eish ('Covenant of Fire'),
כִּי מִדָּתוֹ הַצִּמְצוּם וְהַגְּבוּרָה
for his attribute is constriction (Tzimtzum) and divine strength (Gevurah)
לְהִתְגַּבֵּר נֶגֶד כָּל תַּאֲווֹת וַחֲמוּדוֹת רָעוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם.
to conquer and subdue all base passions and corrupt cravings in the world.
וְהַיְינוּ אֵשׁ אוֹכְלָה אֵשׁ הַתַּאֲוָה וְהַיֵּצֶר הָרָע.
And this is a supernal consuming fire devouring the base fire of lust and the evil inclination.
וְהֻוצְרַךְ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לְהִתְאַחֵר עַד מֵאָה שָׁנָה
And our father Abraham was required to wait until the age of one hundred years
כְּדֵי שֶׁיֵּצֵא יִצְחָק בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה יְתֵירָה,
so that Isaac would emerge into the world in extraordinary holiness and purity,
כִּדְאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מו):
as taught in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 46): "'
קִנָּמוֹן אֲנִי מַעֲמִיד בָּעוֹלָם וְכוּלֵי',
''I am establishing cinnamon in the world, etc.'
כָּךְ מִשֶּׁנִּצְרַר דָּמוֹ, מִשֶּׁבָּטַל יִצְרוֹ, מִשֶּׁבָּטְלָה תַּאֲוָתוֹ וְכוּלֵי".
So it was only after his blood was bound up, after his base inclination was nullified, and after bodily desire was extinguished, etc.'
וְיָדוּעַ כִּי הַקִּנָּמוֹן מְעֻלֶּה בְּרֵיחוֹ,
And it is known that cinnamon is supreme in its fragrant aroma,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת סג.):
as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Shabbat 63a):
שֶׁמֵּעֲצֵי קִנָּמוֹן שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, כְּשֶׁהָיוּ מַסִּיקִין מֵהֶן, רֵיחָן נוֹדֵף בְּכָל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
that when they kindled the wood of cinnamon trees in Jerusalem, its fragrant scent wafted throughout the entire Land of Israel.
וּקְדוּשַׁת הַבְּרִית נִקְרָא רֵיחַ טוֹב,
And the sanctification of the Covenant is termed a sweet fragrance,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (עֵירוּבִין כא:): "'הַדּוּדָאִים נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ' – אֵלּוּ בַּחוּרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא טָעֲמוּ טַעַם חֵטְא".
as written in Eruvin (21b): ''The mandrakes yield fragrance'—these are the youths of Israel who have never tasted the taste of sin.'
וּלְשׁוֹן "בַּחוּרֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל" מוֹרֶה עַל פְּגָם זֶה שֶׁגּוֹרֵם הַבַּחֲרוּת
And the phrase 'youths of Israel' denotes this specific vulnerability induced during youth,
וּמִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ,
wherein one rises and conquers his inclination,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נוֹתְנִים רֵיחַ טוֹב.
and through this they emit a sublime, holy fragrance.
וְיִצְחָק הָיָה הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּימּוֹל לִשְׁמוֹנָה
And Isaac was the very first who was circumcised on the eighth day
וְנִימּוֹל בִּקְדוּשַׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
and circumcised into the sacred covenantal status of Israel.

h: Yaakov and the Completion of Shabbat

p: וְיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת,
And our father Jacob corresponds to the holiness of Shabbat,
דְּאִיתָא (בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא):
as stated in Bereishit Rabbah (parashah 11): "
אַבְרָהָם שֶׁאֵין כָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי, יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵי".
'Abraham, regarding whom the observance of Shabbat is not explicitly recorded, etc.; Jacob, regarding whom the observance of Shabbat is recorded, etc.'
וְהוּא, שֶׁאַף שֶׁגַּם אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק שָׁמְרוּ הַשַּׁבָּת,
And the meaning is: even though Abraham and Isaac certainly observed Shabbat,
שֶׁהֲרֵי קִיֵּים אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם כָּל הַתּוֹרָה,
since Abraham our father, peace be upon him, fulfilled the entirety of the Torah,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם לֹא נִכְתַּב בָּהֶם שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת בְּפֵירוּשׁ וּבִפְרָט.
nonetheless, the observance of Shabbat was not explicitly and specifically recorded concerning them.
וְעַל כֵּן נִיתְּנָה לָהֶם הָאָרֶץ בְּמִדָּה,
And therefore the Land of Israel was given unto them with defined boundaries and measure,
וְהַיְינוּ כָּל זְמַן הֱיוֹתָם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל;
meaning strictly so long as they remained physically within the Land of Israel;
אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ בִּפְרָט מִצְוַת שַׁבָּת:
however Jacob, regarding whom the commandment of Shabbat is explicitly documented: "
וַיִּחַן אֶת פְּנֵי הָעִיר" – שֶׁקָּבַע תְּחוּמִין מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
'and he encamped before the city' (Genesis 33:18)—meaning he established Sabbath boundary limits (techumin) while it was yet day,
וְהַיְינוּ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה שֶׁקָּבַע מָקוֹם לִקְדוּשַּׁת שַׁבָּת.
namely the two thousand cubits wherein he established a designated realm for the sanctity of Shabbat.
וְהַטַּעַם מֵאַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לִתְחוּם שַׁבָּת
And the reason for two thousand cubits constituting the Sabbath boundary
הוּא דְּמִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה תַּ"ק (חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת) פְּעָמִים,
is that the heavenly measure of goodness exceeds the measure of retribution by five hundredfold;
וּמָצִינוּ בַּהַהֵיפֶךְ שֶׁתּוֹפֵס אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
and we find conversely that a negative presence occupies four cubits,
כְּמוֹ בְּמֵת וְזוֹנָה וּמִינוּת (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יז.) וּבְרֵיחַ רַע (בְּרָכוֹת כה.),
such as regarding a corpse, a harlot, heresy (Avodah Zarah 17a), and a foul odor (Berakhot 25a);
וּמִדָּה טוֹבָה מְרֻבָּה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת פְּעָמִים קוֹנֶה אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה.
and the measure of divine goodness exceeding by five hundred times acquires two thousand cubits (4 × 500 = 2,000).
וְעַל כֵּן זָכָה יַעֲקֹב וְיָרַשׁ הָעוֹלָם שֶׁלֹּא בְּמִדָּה,
And therefore Jacob merited and inherited the world without bound or limitation,
וּכְתִיב בּוֹ: "וּפָרַצְתָּ יָמָּה וָקֵדְמָה וְגוֹמֵר",
and it is written of him (Genesis 28:14): 'And you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, etc.,'
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיּוּכַל לִפְרוֹץ קְדוּשָׁתוֹ בְּכָל מָקוֹם אַף שֶׁלֹּא בָּאָרֶץ,
meaning that he is empowered to burst forth his holiness into every place, even beyond the geographic borders of the Land,
שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיִּהְיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל, הַשְּׁכִינָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה בְּתוֹכָם.
such that wherever Israel may be dispersed, the Holy Shechinah abides in their midst.
וְעִיקַּר זְמַן הַשְׁרָאַת הַשְּׁכִינָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא בְּיוֹם שַׁבָּת,
And the primary moment for the indwelling of the Shechinah within Israel is on the Sabbath day,
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, סג עַמּוּד ב):
as taught in the holy Zohar (Part II, 63b): "'
אַל יֵצֵא אִישׁ מִמְּקֹמוֹ', וְרָזָא דְּמִלָּה דִּכְתִיב 'בָּרוּךְ כְּבוֹד ה' מִמְּקוֹמוֹ'",
''Let no man go out of his place' (Exodus 16:29), and the inner secret of this word is written: 'Blessed be the glory of Hashem from His place' (Ezekiel 3:12),'
וְהַיְינוּ שְׁכִינְתָּא תַּתָּאָה שֶׁשּׁוֹרָה בְּלֵב יִשְׂרָאֵל.
namely the lower Shechinah (Malchut) that rests within the Jewish heart.
וְאִיתָא (תִּקּוּנֵי הַזֹּהַר תִּקּוּן ו): "זַכָּאָה מַאן דִּמְתַקֵּן לָהּ דִּירָה נָאָה בְּלִבֵּיהּ",
And it is written (Tikkunei HaZohar, Tikkun 6): 'Fortunate is he who prepares for Her a beautiful dwelling in his heart,'
וְהַיְינוּ בְּשַׁבָּת,
and that refers specifically to Shabbat.
דְּאִיתָא (בְּרָכוֹת ח.): שֶׁאֵין לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ אֶלָּא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה,
For it is taught (Berakhot 8a) that the Holy One, blessed be He, has nothing in His world except the four cubits of Halakhah,
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁשָּׁם שׁוֹרָה הַשְּׁכִינָה מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
meaning that there the Shechinah resides ever since the Day the Temple was destroyed.
וְאָמַר רַבֵּינוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ זְצוּקַ"ל
And our holy Master (the Rebbe of Peshischa), of blessed memory, explained
שֶׁהַפֵּירוּשׁ הוּא: מִי שֶׁמִּתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ וּפוֹרֵשׁ מֵהָאִיסּוּר כַּהֲלָכָה
that the meaning is: whoever conquers his evil inclination and withdraws from forbidden matters according to Halakhah
וּמְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם,
and accepts upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven,
זֶה נִקְרָא אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה,
this is what is titled 'the four cubits of Halakhah,'
כִּי זֶה עִיקַּר הַמְּכֻוָּון מִדְּבַר הֲלָכָה.
for this constitutes the essential objective of every halakhic teaching.
וְהוּא עוֹשֶׂה דִּירָה לַשְּׁכִינְתָּא בְּלִבֵּיהּ,
And he constructs an abode for the Shechinah in his heart;
